---
title: "Euler 124"
format: html
date: '2026-08-18'

---
Kinda cheating - `numbers` have a function for finding radicals

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(numbers)

radicals <- tibble(n = 1:100000)
radicals <- radicals |>
rowwise() |>
mutate(rad_n = radical(n))

radicals_sorted <- radicals |> arrange(rad_n)
answer <- radicals_sorted[10000,]
```


Rather than cheating directly, we can cheat indirectly:
```{r}
own_radical <- function(n){
  primeFactors(n) |> unique() |> prod()
}

```

Or, vectorized:

```{r}
own_vect_radical <- function(v){
  lapply(X = v, FUN = primeFactors) |> 
  lapply(FUN = unique) |> 
  lapply(FUN = prod) |> 
  unlist()
}
```

Or, somewhat, simpler:

```{r}
simpler_own_vect_radical <- function(v){
  vapply(
    X = v,
    FUN = \(x) prod(unique(numbers::primeFactors(x))),
    FUN.VALUE = numeric(1)
)
}
```
